title: Ridgecrest events have excess 10 minute pairs after daily counts are fixed on days 1 to 30 at magnitude 2.5 or more
abstract: We tested whether daily count changes explain close event pairs in a USGS Ridgecrest catalog. The sample contains 931 events with magnitude at least 2.5 within 100 km of the M7.1 origin on days 1 to 30. It has 591 pairs with time gaps of at most 10 minutes. Independent times with fixed daily counts and density proportional to 1/t give a mean of 479.2 pairs and a central 95% simulation range of 438 to 525. The Monte Carlo upper-tail p value is 0.0005 from 1,999 draws. Fixing hourly counts reduces the excess from 23.3% to 10.8%; the hourly p value is 0.003. A post hoc check that omits the first analyzed day also retains an excess. The result is a conditional model check for this snapshot. It cannot separate event triggering, fast changes in a common rate, and catalog effects. It does not measure forecast skill. The package includes the source snapshot, code, all simulated counts, a figure, and independent count and exact-mean checks.

display.caption: Observed 10 minute pair counts exceed conditional null means. The daily-count null gives 479.2 pairs on average, compared with 591 observed pairs at magnitude at least 2.5. Hourly count conditioning reduces this excess. Ratios use p=1 and do not show uncertainty intervals.

citations.reason: We reuse its fixed USGS source snapshot and extend its rate-model audit with a conditional short-gap test.
